chapters.chapter_title: Lesson 10: Write from Dictation and Listening: Fill in the Blanks

estimated_study_time.text: Plan for about 2 hours of focused study.

chapter_summary.text: This lesson practises Listening: Fill in the blanks and Write from dictation. It focuses on listening, writing, and speaking skills, including following spoken sequencing, understanding academic vocabulary, writing from dictation, correct grammar and spelling, natural-rate speech, intonation, pronunciation, stress, and timed conditions.

evidence_spans.quote:
This lesson provides skills practice for the PTE Academic item types Write from dictation and Listening: Fill in 
the blanks.

Listening
• Identifying words and phrases appropriate to the context
• Understanding academic vocabulary
• Comprehending explicit and implicit information
• Following an oral sequencing of information

Writing
• Writing from dictation
• Using words and phrases appropriate to the context
• Using correct grammar
• Using correct spelling

Speaking
• Speaking at a natural rate
• Producing fluent speech
• Using correct intonation
• Using correct pronunciation
• Using correct stress
• Speaking under timed conditions

learning_objectives.text: Practise the listening, writing, and speaking skills listed for the lesson.

evidence_spans.quote:
By the end of this lesson, test takers will have: 
➤	 Practiced the listening, writing and speaking skills listed above

learning_objectives.text: Analyze the rubrics, format, and test-taking strategies for Listening: Fill in the blanks and Write from dictation.

evidence_spans.quote:
➤	 Analyzed the rubrics and format of these items
➤	 Analyzed test-taking strategies for these items

This lesson provides skills practice for the PTE Academic item types Write from dictation and Listening: Fill in 
the blanks.

learning_objectives.text: Complete practice items under timed conditions and review feedback on those practice items.

evidence_spans.quote:
➤	 Completed practice items under timed conditions
➤	 Reviewed feedback to practice items

learning_objectives.text: Develop awareness of how context, meaning, and spelling help distinguish homophones.

evidence_spans.quote:
in English there are many words that have the same pronunciation but 
different spellings and that the spelling of such words depends on the context and the meaning.

meaning.text: An item type that tests the ability to listen for missing words in a recording and type the words into a transcription; it assesses both listening and writing skills.

evidence_spans.quote:
Fill in the blanks is an item type that tests your ability to listen for missing words in a recording and type the 
words into a transcription. It assesses both listening and writing skills.

meaning.text: An item type that tests the ability to understand and remember a sentence heard, then write it exactly as heard using correct spelling; it assesses both listening and writing skills.

evidence_spans.quote:
Write from dictation is an item type that tests your ability to understand and remember a sentence you hear and 
then write exactly as you hear it using correct spelling. It assesses both listening and writing skills.

meaning.text: Words that have the same pronunciation but different spellings; their correct spelling depends on context and meaning.

evidence_spans.quote:
in English there are many words that have the same pronunciation but 
different spellings and that the spelling of such words depends on the context and the meaning.

meaning.text: For Fill in the blanks, content is scored by counting right words with correct spelling; for Write from dictation, content is scored by counting correct words in the response.

evidence_spans.quote:
Your score on Fill in the blanks is based on content. Content is scored by counting the number of right words 
with correct spelling in your response.

Your score on Write from dictation is based on content. Content is scored by counting the number of correct 
words in your response.

explanation.text: For both item types, an important skill is remaining focused while listening and closely following the sequence of a spoken text.

evidence_spans.quote:
an important skill for both of these items types is the ability to remain focused 
while listening, and to closely follow the sequence of a spoken text.

core_lessons.title: Know The Fill In The Blanks Format

explanation.text: In Listening: Fill in the blanks, instructions appear at the top of the screen, a seven-second countdown precedes the automatic recording, and the response is entered into up to seven blanks in a transcription.

evidence_spans.quote:
Instructions are presented at the top of the computer screen. The instructions for this item type are always the  
same.

In the audio status box, the status will count down from seven seconds. Then a recording will play 
automatically.

A transcription of the recording with up to seven blanks follows. To respond, type the missing words into the 
blanks.

core_lessons.title: Know The Write From Dictation Format

explanation.text: In Write from dictation, the learner hears a sentence once, types the sentence in the response box exactly as heard, and writes as much of the sentence as possible.

evidence_spans.quote:
You will hear a sentence. Type the sentence in the box below exactly as you hear it. Write as much of the 
sentence as you can. You will hear the sentence only once.
A response box follows. Use this space to type the sentence.

explanation.text: When a word has the same pronunciation as another word, context and meaning determine the correct spelling.

evidence_spans.quote:
it was important to listen to and understand the meaning of the context in order to know which was the 
correct spelling in each case
the spelling of such words depends on the context and the meaning.

explanation.text: After completing listening texts, learners should check that their sentences make sense and use correct grammatical forms and spelling.

evidence_spans.quote:
check 
their own responses to make sure that the sentences make sense, and that they have used correct 
grammatical forms and spelling.

explanation.text: During paired practice, learners should sit so they are not facing each other, because this imitates test conditions in which there are no visual clues such as lip movements, facial clues, or gestures.

evidence_spans.quote:
test takers should sit so that they are not facing each other. Explain that this is to imitate test 
conditions in which test takers will have no visual clues (lip movements, other facial clues, gestures, etc)

example.text: Prompt: The ___ of the financial crisis are still being felt around the world. Answer: effects. Check: the sentence is about results of a crisis, so the spelling is effects, not affect.

explanation.text: The lesson answer key gives the completed sentence as: The effects of the financial crisis are still being felt around the world.

evidence_spans.quote: The effects of the financial crisis are still being felt around the world.

example.text: Prompt heard once: Before submitting your report, check that the bibliography is complete. Learner response: Before submitting your report, check that the bibliography is complete.

explanation.text: In the practice item, the reader reads each sentence once only, pauses for 10 seconds, and the listener writes as much as they can remember.

evidence_spans.quote:
Read each sentence aloud to your partner once only. Then pause for 10 seconds to let your partner 
write the sentence.

Listen carefully to the sentences that your partner reads aloud. Write as much of each sentence as 
you can remember in the space below.

misconception.text: For homophones, hearing the sound alone is enough to know the correct spelling.

correction.text: For homophones, the correct spelling depends on context and meaning.

evidence_spans.quote: the spelling of such words depends on the context and the meaning.

misconception.text: In Write from dictation, it is acceptable to write a rough paraphrase of the sentence.

correction.text: In Write from dictation, the sentence should be typed exactly as heard, and the learner should write as much of the sentence as possible.

evidence_spans.quote:
Type the sentence in the box below exactly as you hear it. Write as much of the 
sentence as you can.

question.text: Choose the correct word: Many experts were initially skeptical and could not ___ the key hypothesis. Options: accept / except.
Write the full sentence from memory after one reading: The project involved a number of discrete studies.

answer.text: The project involved a number of discrete studies.

question.text: For Listening: Fill in the blanks, what should you type into the blanks?

answer.text: Type the missing words in each blank.

question.text: Choose the correct word: It is unclear ___ the government will successfully ___ the current political storm. Options: whether/weather or weather/whether.

review_checklist.text: I can stay focused while listening and follow the sequence of a spoken text.
I can use context and meaning to choose the correct spelling of homophones.
I can check my responses for meaning, grammar, and spelling after listening.
I can practise Write from dictation by listening once, remembering accurately, and writing as much of the sentence as I can.
I can practise Listening: Fill in the blanks by listening for missing words and entering the correctly spelled words.
